questions.title: Section A: Multiple Choice, Matching, Terminology and True/False

subQuestions.questionText: A person who recognises a business opportunity and is willing to take a risk:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
An entrepreneur is a person who recognises business opportunities and takes calculated risks to start and run a business.

subQuestions.questionText: ONE of the following statements regarding selling is NOT CORRECT:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Selling is short-term and focuses on existing products. Long-term planning based on new products for the future is characteristic of marketing, not selling.

options.B: Marketing management is based on sales volume
options.C: Focus is on the needs of sellers
options.D: Planning is long-term, based on new products for the future

subQuestions.questionText: ... occurs at the point where the market supply and the market demand curves meet.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
Market equilibrium is the point where supply and demand curves intersect, establishing the equilibrium price and quantity.

subQuestions.questionText:
Cooperative marketing has the following advantages for farmers:
(i) Provides better chances of negotiating a good price
(ii) Ensures easy access to funding
(iii) Prices of products fluctuate and producers are affected
(iv) Markets are preserved for members
Choose the CORRECT combination:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
The correct advantages of cooperative marketing are (i), (ii) and (iv). Statement (iii) is a disadvantage, not an advantage.

subQuestions.questionText: An example of an internal force that affects a farming business:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Labour demands for higher wages is an internal force originating from within the business. Natural forces, market prices and lifestyle changes are external forces.

options.A: Natural forces like hail and floods
options.C: The drop of the milk price in the market

subQuestions.questionText: ONE of the following is NOT a function of land:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Land does NOT depreciate over time - it appreciates. The other options are all valid functions of land.

options.A: Acts as a store of wealth
options.C: Enables the production of food, fibre and fuel

subQuestions.questionText: ... is the main component of a cash flow statement.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
Income is the main component of a cash flow statement, which tracks money flowing in and out of a business. Net worth, assets and liabilities are components of a balance sheet.

subQuestions.questionText: The use of machinery to replace human labour:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Mechanisation is the process of replacing human/animal labour with machinery to increase efficiency and productivity.

subQuestions.questionText: An example of a qualitative characteristic in animals:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Gender of offspring is a qualitative characteristic (categorical, not measurable on a continuous scale). Weight gain, milk production and growth rate are quantitative characteristics that can be measured.

subQuestions.questionText: ... is the pattern of inheritance that controls the fur coat colour in rabbits with the alleles C, Ch, Cch and c.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Multiple alleles refers to inheritance involving more than two alleles for a single trait, as seen in rabbit coat colour with C, Ch, Cch and c alleles.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the description in COLUMN A with a term from COLUMN B: Cooperatives market their goods in large quantities for more bargaining powers. (Column B options: A hedging, B qualitative, C motivation, D quantitative, E contract, F depreciation, G economy of scale, H appreciation)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: G - Economy of scale (2 marks)
Economy of scale refers to cost advantages obtained from large-scale production/marketing, giving cooperatives bargaining power.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the description in COLUMN A with a term from COLUMN B: Entering into future contracts to ensure a secure market and price.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - Hedging (2 marks)
Hedging is the practice of entering into futures contracts to lock in prices and reduce the risk of price fluctuations.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the description in COLUMN A with a term from COLUMN B: The value of assets increasing over time.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: H - Appreciation (2 marks)
Appreciation is the increase in the value of assets over time, opposite to depreciation.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the description in COLUMN A with a term from COLUMN B: Providing incentives and recognition of work done with rewards.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - Motivation (2 marks)
Motivation involves providing incentives and recognition to encourage employees and improve productivity.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the description in COLUMN A with a term from COLUMN B: The genetic characteristics that give rise to a range of phenotypes from one extreme to the other.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - Quantitative (2 marks)
Quantitative characteristics show continuous variation across a range of phenotypes (e.g. weight, milk yield), as opposed to qualitative traits which are categorical.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: A measure of how much the supply or demand of a product changes with a change in price.
subQuestions.memoText:
Price elasticity (2 marks)
Price elasticity measures the responsiveness of supply or demand to changes in price.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: The activity that involves the combination and co-ordination of human, physical and financial resources.
subQuestions.memoText:
Management (2 marks)
Management is the process of coordinating human, physical and financial resources to achieve organisational goals.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: The passing on of traits from generation to generation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Heredity (2 marks)
Heredity is the genetic transmission of traits/characteristics from parents to offspring across generations.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: Measuring genetic characteristics by using computer technology.
subQuestions.memoText:
Biometrics (2 marks)
Biometrics involves the statistical/computational analysis of biological/genetic data using computer technology.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: The picking of individual cultivars based on the records of their respective offspring.
subQuestions.memoText:
Progeny selection (2 marks)
Progeny selection is the method of selecting parent breeding stock based on the performance and records of their offspring.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) to make the statement TRUE: A marketing plan is a tool that helps a farmer to evaluate the business for future prospects.
subQuestions.memoText:
SWOT analysis (1 mark)
A SWOT analysis (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats) is the tool used to evaluate a business for future prospects. A marketing plan focuses on marketing strategies.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) to make the statement TRUE: Management refers to the physical endeavour performed in expectation of remuneration.
subQuestions.memoText:
Labour (1 mark)
Labour refers to the physical/mental effort performed in exchange for payment. Management is the coordination of resources.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) to make the statement TRUE: Prepotency refers to the expression of one gene that is controlled by another pair of genes.
subQuestions.memoText:
Epistasis (1 mark)
Epistasis is when one gene's expression is masked or controlled by another gene at a different locus. Prepotency refers to an individual's ability to pass on traits to offspring.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) to make the statement TRUE: A sudden change in the genetic composition of an organism is known as selection.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mutation (1 mark)
Mutation is a sudden change in the DNA/genetic composition of an organism. Selection is the process of choosing individuals for breeding.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) to make the statement TRUE: A gene is a thread-like structure made up of DNA molecules.
subQuestions.memoText:
Chromosome (1 mark)
A chromosome is the thread-like structure made of DNA. A gene is a specific segment of DNA on a chromosome that codes for a trait.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the functions of agricultural marketing represented by B and D. (Refer to the schematic representation of marketing in agriculture in the question paper. B = Safekeeping of products until they are needed; D = Movement of products from the farm to the consumer)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: B - Storage
Mark 2: D - Transportation
[Award 1 mark each for correct identification of marketing functions]

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate TWO guidelines that farmers should consider when performing marketing function C (packaging).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Product identification
• Recyclability/biodegradability
• Containment/easy handling
• Protection
• Should improve shelf life
• Health risk/free from chemicals/cleanliness
• Appeal to the target market

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO advantages of marketing function A (processing) to the consumer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Provides job opportunities
• Easy to handle the product/convenience
• Can buy farm products and keep for longer at home
• Product availability in all seasons/ensures food security
• Provides quality improved products
• Makes the products more appealing

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify in graphs A and B above the curves that represent EACH of the following:
(a) Demand
(b) Supply
(Graph A shows curve G→A→B→C; Graph B shows curve F→E→D)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Demand - H (F E D) (1 mark) [Downward sloping curve in Graph B]
(b) Supply - G (A B C) (1 mark) [Upward sloping curve in Graph A]

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 2.2.1(a). (Demand)
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE of the following (2 marks):
• The higher the price of a product, the lower the demand
• The lower the price of a product, the higher the demand
• There is an inverse relationship between price and demand
• Has a negative/downward slope to the right

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO factors that influence demand of agricultural products.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Price of the product/price expectations
• Quality of the product
• Consumer taste and preferences
• Fashion/advertising
• Change in consumer income
• Number of consumers
• Socio-economic factors/buying power
• Legislation
• Research
• Price of substitutes/competitive or complementary products
• Festive season
• Usefulness of the product

subQuestions.questionText: Deduce the relationship between price and quantity from graph A above (supply curve).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE of the following (2 marks):
• The higher the price, the more the quantity supplied
• The lower the price, the lower the quantity supplied
[There is a direct/positive relationship between price and quantity supplied]

subQuestions.questionText:
Write down the letter (A–D) that represents the following entrepreneurial success factors:
(a) Innovation
(b) Interpersonal skills
(c) Risk taking
(Refer to the schematic representation of entrepreneurial success factors in the question paper. A = Able to negotiate contracts with markets; B = Buying new equipment to increase production; C = Ability to generate new ideas; D = Understanding of taxation and exchange rates)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Innovation - C (1 mark) [Ability to generate new ideas]
(b) Interpersonal skills - A (1 mark) [Able to negotiate contracts with markets]
(c) Risk taking - B (1 mark) [Buying new equipment to increase production]

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the marketing approaches represented by A, B and C above. (A = One offer/strategy appealing to most consumers; B = Dividing target market into different portions; C = Selling pasteurised goat milk to consumers allergic to cow milk)
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Mass marketing (1 mark) [One strategy for everyone]
B - Multi-segment marketing (1 mark) [Different segments targeted differently]
C - Niche marketing (1 mark) [Targeting a specific small segment]

subQuestions.questionText: Name the marketing process in the flow chart above. (Producer → Processing → Distribution → Retailer → Consumer)
subQuestions.memoText:
Agri-business / Marketing / Supply-demand chain (1 mark)
This represents the agri-business value chain from producer to final consumer.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate TWO costs visible in the flow chart above that might influence the high price at STAGE 4 (Retailer), except for production.
subQuestions.memoText:
Both of the following (1 mark each):
• Processing costs
• Distribution/transportation costs

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO factors that could hamper the marketing of the product at STAGE 3 (Distribution).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Accidents/delays
• Poor infrastructure/bad roads
• Theft
• Perishability/spoilage/damage of the product
• High cost of fuel

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate ONE way to streamline and improve the marketing process stated in QUESTION 2.5.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE of the following (1 mark):
• Improve road infrastructure
• Improve access to market information
• Provide storage facilities
• Provide access to finance
• Use cold storage and refrigerated transport
• Grading/standardisation of products to facilitate marketing/pricing
• Processing products close to where they are produced
• Combining loads with other producers

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO advantages of the marketing channel in the statement above (fresh produce markets via market agent) for the farmer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Large volumes can be sold
• Farmer takes advantage of higher price in times of short supply
• Farmer can employ an agent to perform the task of marketing

subQuestions.questionText: The use of an agent increases the marketing cost for the farmer. Justify this statement.
subQuestions.memoText:
The farmer pays the commission to the agent (1 mark)
Market agents charge a commission/fee for selling produce on behalf of the farmer, increasing the overall marketing cost.

subQuestions.questionText: Name the marketing system that makes use of the channel above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Free marketing (1 mark)
Fresh produce markets operate as a free marketing system where prices are determined by supply and demand.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate TWO roles of legislation in agricultural marketing.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Increases market access to all participants
• Controls sale and export of perishable products
• Sets and maintains national standards
• Promotes food safety
• Regulates market agents and improves their functioning
• Promotes a fair, accessible and sustainable market place for consumer products and services
• Prevents unfair marketing and business practices

subQuestions.questionText: Name the component of a business plan containing particulars of the business owner.
subQuestions.memoText:
Title page (1 mark)
The title page is the first component of a business plan and contains particulars/details of the business owner(s).

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons for drawing up a business plan.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Document the business idea
• Test the feasibility and economic viability of a business
• Determine the financial needs of the business
• Secure funding for the business
• Guide daily operations
• Ensure effective business management
• Allow the farmer to foresee problems
• Gain knowledge about marketing opportunities/competitors
• Reposition the business to deal with changes in the market

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the economic characteristic shown in the graph above. (Refer to the graph showing total yield against quantity of inputs in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
The law of diminishing returns (1 mark)
The graph shows total yield increasing at a decreasing rate as inputs increase, which is the law of diminishing returns.

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the implication of the economic characteristic identified in QUESTION 3.1.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Output will initially increase at an increasing rate with increase of input
Mark 2: A further increase in input will result in increased output at a decreasing rate
[Eventually additional inputs yield smaller and smaller increases in output]
subQuestions.topic: Production Factors - Law of Diminishing Returns

subQuestions.questionText: Compare the output response with regard to the quantity of inputs that increases from 5 to 10 and from 10 to 15.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: 5 to 10: An input of 5 units resulted in an output of 10 units / output increases at an increasing rate with an increase in inputs
Mark 2: 10 to 15: An input of 5 units resulted in an output of 5 units / output increases at a decreasing rate with an increase in inputs

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO measures the farmer can take to improve the productivity of land.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Development of disease-resistant cultivars/breeds
• The use of fertilisers/manure/compost
• Appropriate use of land/better care of agricultural land
• Adapting to/use of scientific methods/technology/precision/organic farming/correct cultivation methods/crop rotation
• Consolidation of small/uneconomic farming units
• Restoring land potential/resting land/correct land utilisation
• Responsible application of chemicals/pesticides/herbicides
• Mechanisation
• Adapting to appropriate policies/legislation
• Water provision/management/irrigation

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the management strategy undertaken by the farmer to reduce the impact of risk shown in the picture above. (Picture shows a farming enterprise with multiple types of agricultural activities.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Diversification (1 mark)
Diversification reduces risk by spreading farm operations across multiple enterprises.

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 3.2.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
There are different production enterprises on the farm (1 mark)
The picture shows multiple farming activities (crops, livestock, poultry, etc.) which is characteristic of diversification.

subQuestions.questionText: Name the risk management strategy when the cost of a farming enterprise is distributed equally among the group of farmers.
subQuestions.memoText:
Risk-sharing (1 mark)
Risk-sharing distributes risk and costs among multiple parties (e.g. cooperatives, partnerships, insurance pools).

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the source of the risk that may be due to a disease outbreak.
subQuestions.memoText:
Production risk / Technical risk (1 mark - any one)
Disease outbreaks affect production output, classified as production or technical risk.

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO management principles a farm manager could employ to deal with risks.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Planning
• Organising and coordination
• Implementation
• Control/monitoring

subQuestions.questionText: Define the term contract.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: A legally binding document
Mark 2: between the employer and employee
[A contract is a legally binding agreement between two or more parties outlining terms and conditions]

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the type of farm worker who has to sign the contract above based on the term of employment. (Contract states: Duration of contract: 2 January 2021 to retirement)
subQuestions.memoText:
Permanent / Full-time worker (1 mark)
A contract running from a start date until retirement signifies permanent/full-time employment.

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason to support the answer to QUESTION 3.3.2.
subQuestions.memoText:
The contract will terminate at retirement (1 mark)
This indicates long-term/permanent employment until the worker retires.

subQuestions.questionText:
Name the labour legislation that has been violated by the employer in EACH of the following sections of the contract above:
(a) Number 7 (Working hours: 06:00–18:00; Leave: Five days paid leave per annum)
(b) Number 8 (Protective clothing: None)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Basic Conditions of Employment Act / BCEA (Act No. 75 of 1997) (1 mark) [12-hour working day exceeds the legal limit; only 5 days leave is below minimum]
(b) Occupational Health and Safety Act / OHSA (Act No. 85 of 1993) (1 mark) [No protective clothing violates safety regulations]

subQuestions.questionText: Identify, in the contract above, TWO reasons that may lead to the movement of farm workers from the farm to other industries.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Poor working conditions / less leave days (only 5 days)
• Low wages/salaries (R2 300 per month)
• Longer working hours (06:00 to 18:00 = 12 hours)
• Lack of protective clothing

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the type of capital represented by A, B and C in the picture above. (A = livestock; B = silos/feed storage structures; C = feed/hay)
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Movable capital (1 mark) [Livestock can be moved]
B - Fixed capital (1 mark) [Silos are permanently fixed structures]
C - Working/floating/production capital (1 mark) [Feed is consumed during production]

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate TWO methods by which a farmer can create more capital.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Production / own capital
• Savings
• Credit / loans
• Grants

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO problems associated with capital as a production factor.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Scarcity / difficult access to capital
• Expensive / high cost / interest rates
• Depreciation
• Law of diminishing returns
• Undercapitalisation
• Overcapitalisation
• High risk

subQuestions.questionText: Name the financial statement above. (Table showing assets and liabilities of a farming business for the year ending 28 February 2021.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Balance sheet (1 mark)
A balance sheet shows the assets, liabilities and net worth of a business at a specific date.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify A in the financial statement above. (A is the heading for: Positive bank balance, Farm produce sold, Growing crops - subtotal R31 000)
subQuestions.memoText:
Current / Short-term assets (1 mark)
Current assets are assets that can be converted to cash within one year (cash, produce sold, growing crops).

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the value of B in the financial statement above. Show ALL calculations. (B = TOTAL LIABILITIES; Current liabilities R55 000; Medium-term liabilities R340 000; Long-term liabilities R570 000)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: R55 000 + R340 000 + R570 000
Mark 2: = R965 000
[Total Liabilities = sum of current, medium-term and long-term liabilities]

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the net worth of the farming business above. Include the formula. (Total assets = R1 861 000; Total liabilities = R965 000)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Formula: Net worth = Total assets − Total liabilities
Mark 2: Substitution: = R1 861 000 − R965 000
Mark 3: Answer: = R896 000
[Net worth represents the owner's equity in the business]

subQuestions.questionText: Identify, in the flow chart above, TWO common ancestors of individuals A and B. (Refer to the schematic representation of line breeding showing individuals 1-9 and offspring A, B, C in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• 1
• 4
• 5
[These individuals appear in the ancestral lines of both A and B in the line breeding chart]

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the relationship between individuals 2 and 3.
subQuestions.memoText:
Siblings / Brothers and sisters (1 mark)
Individuals 2 and 3 share the same parents, making them siblings.

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO advantages of line breeding.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Leads to stronger prepotency in the progeny
• Undesirable recessive characteristics can be identified/uncovered for elimination from the herd
• Favourable characteristics of an outstanding ancestor are quickly laid down in the progeny
• Progeny display a high degree of homozygosity

subQuestions.questionText: State the number of generations obtained from parents 1 and 2 in the pedigree diagram above. (Refer to the pedigree diagram showing inheritance of coat colour in goats with individuals 1-11 across multiple generations.)
subQuestions.memoText:
3 (1 mark)
The pedigree shows three generations: F1 generation (individuals 3, 4, 5), F2 generation (individuals 6, 7, 8), and F3 generation (individuals 9, 10, 11).

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the number of white male individuals in the pedigree diagram in QUESTION 4.2.
subQuestions.memoText:
4 (1 mark)
White (unshaded) male individuals are: 3, 5, 8 and 10 = 4 white males.

subQuestions.questionText:
Determine the genotypes of EACH of the following individuals:
(a) 1
(b) 5
(KEY: Unshaded/White = d, Shaded/Dark = D)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) 1 - Dd (1 mark) [Individual 1 is dark/shaded but has white offspring (3 and 5), so must be heterozygous Dd]
(b) 5 - dd (1 mark) [Individual 5 is white/unshaded, which is the recessive trait, so must be homozygous recessive dd]

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to the pedigree diagram in QUESTION 4.2 and indicate whether the following individuals are homozygous or heterozygous:
(a) 6
(b) 10
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) 6 - Heterozygous (1 mark) [Individual 6 is dark/shaded but has white offspring, so must be Dd]
(b) 10 - Homozygous (1 mark) [Individual 10 is white/unshaded, which is recessive, so must be homozygous dd]

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 4.2.4(b). (Individual 10 is homozygous)
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE of the following (2 marks):
• The offspring is white in colour which is recessive and can only be expressed in homozygous condition
• White recessive pure breed
[Recessive traits can only be expressed when both alleles are recessive (homozygous recessive dd)]

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the sex chromosomes in male cattle.
subQuestions.memoText:
XY (1 mark)
Male cattle have heterogametic sex chromosomes XY (one X and one Y chromosome).

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the sex chromosomes in female cattle.
subQuestions.memoText:
XX (1 mark)
Female cattle have homogametic sex chromosomes XX (two X chromosomes).

subQuestions.questionText: In certain species of plants blue flower colour (B) is dominant over purple (b). A plant with heterozygous blue flowers was crossed with a homozygous purple-flowered plant. Draw a Punnett square to indicate the result of a cross between the two plants.
subQuestions.memoText:
Punnett square cross: Bb × bb

         |  B  |  b  |
      ---|-----|-----|
      b  | Bb  | bb  |
      ---|-----|-----|
      b  | Bb  | bb  |

Marking rubric (1 mark each, 4 marks total):
• Correct gametes of parent one (B and b) ✓
• Correct gametes of parent two (b and b) ✓
• Correct genotypes of the offspring (Bb, bb, Bb, bb) ✓
• Punnett square (correctly populated with gametes and offspring) ✓

[Result: 50% Bb (blue) : 50% bb (purple) phenotypic ratio of 1:1]

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the type of selection illustrated in the passage above. (Subsistence farmers selected the genetically best bulls for growth, health and fertility.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Artificial selection (1 mark)
Artificial selection is when humans deliberately choose individuals with desirable traits for breeding, as opposed to natural selection.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE animal production characteristic used by subsistence farmers in the passage above for selection purposes.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE of the following (1 mark):
• Growth
• Health
• Fertility

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate how the following aspects were used by the subsistence farmers in the scenario above to improve EACH of the following phenomena on a farm:
(a) Genetic variation
(b) Environmental variation
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Genetic variation: Best bulls for growth/health/fertility were shared (1 mark) [Sharing superior bulls between family/friends introduces new genetics into different herds]
(b) Environmental variation: Utilising the best available pastures / keeping them away from wet/muddy areas (1 mark) [Improving the environment reduces environmental stress and improves expression of genetic potential]

subQuestions.questionText: Draw a combined bar graph of the different characteristics with the numbers obtained and numbers expected. (Data: Large+Tall: Obtained 10, Expected 9; Large+Short: Obtained 3, Expected 3; Small+Tall: Obtained 2, Expected 3; Small+Short: Obtained 1, Expected 1 - all in thousands)
subQuestions.memoText:
Marking criteria/rubric (1 mark each, 6 marks total):
• Correct heading (e.g. 'Different characteristics with the numbers obtained and expected')
• X-axis correctly calibrated with label (Characteristics: L+T, L+S, S+T, S+S)
• Y-axis correctly calibrated with label (Numbers obtained and expected)
• Correct unit (Thousands)
• Combined bar graph (grouped/paired bars showing both Obtained and Expected for each characteristic)
• Accuracy (80%+ correctly plotted)

[Bars should show: L+T (Obtained 10, Expected 9); L+S (Obtained 3, Expected 3); S+T (Obtained 2, Expected 3); S+S (Obtained 1, Expected 1). Y-axis should range 0 to ~12 thousand. Include legend distinguishing Obtained from Expected]

subQuestions.questionText: Deduce, from the graph, the trend of the obtained numbers.
subQuestions.memoText:
The obtained numbers are declining/decreasing (1 mark)
The obtained numbers show a decreasing trend from L+T (10) → L+S (3) → S+T (2) → S+S (1).

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the technique used in the passage above to modify the maize cultivar genetically. (Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) was inserted into the plasma of the maize plant.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Bacterial carriers / Agrobacterium tumefaciens (1 mark)
Bacterial carriers (such as Agrobacterium tumefaciens) are used to transfer foreign DNA (like Bt genes) into plant cells.

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO potential benefits of genetically modified crops to the environment.
subQuestions.memoText:
Both of the following (1 mark each):
• Less chemicals/pesticides/insecticides are used / less susceptible to diseases
• It is target specific [GM crops with Bt only target specific pests, sparing beneficial insects]

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO potential risks of genetically modified crops.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Health risks
• Environmental risks
• Socio-economic risks
